questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are natural numbers?

options.C: Positive whole numbers, zero and negative whole numbers
options.D: Numbers expressible as p/q where q ≠ 0

questions.explanation: Natural numbers are counting numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, ... In the usual school convention, zero is not a natural number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are whole numbers?

options.C: Positive whole numbers, zero and negative whole numbers
options.D: All rational and irrational numbers together

questions.explanation: Whole numbers are natural numbers together with zero: 0, 1, 2, 3, ...

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are integers?

options.C: Positive whole numbers, zero and negative whole numbers: ..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...
options.D: Numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers

questions.explanation: Integers are positive whole numbers, zero and negative whole numbers: ..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are rational numbers?

options.A: Numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers
options.B: Numbers expressible as p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0
options.C: All rational and irrational numbers together
options.D: An integer divisible by 2 without a remainder

questions.explanation: Rational numbers are numbers expressible as p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. Their decimal expansion terminates or repeats.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are irrational numbers?

options.A: Numbers expressible as p/q where q ≠ 0
options.B: Numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers; their decimal expansions are non-terminating and non-repeating
options.C: All rational and irrational numbers together
options.D: Natural numbers greater than 1 having exactly two distinct positive factors

questions.explanation: Irrational numbers cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers; their decimal expansions are non-terminating and non-repeating, e.g. √2 and π.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are real numbers?

options.C: All rational and irrational numbers together

questions.explanation: Real numbers are all rational and irrational numbers together.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is an even number?

options.B: An integer divisible by 2 without a remainder
options.C: A natural number greater than 1 having exactly two distinct positive factors
options.D: A natural number greater than 1 having more than two positive factors

questions.explanation: An even number is an integer divisible by 2 without a remainder.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is an odd number?

options.A: An integer divisible by 2 without a remainder
options.B: An integer not divisible by 2; it leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2
options.C: A natural number greater than 1 having exactly two distinct positive factors
options.D: A number that divides the given number exactly

questions.explanation: An odd number is an integer not divisible by 2; it leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a prime number?

options.A: A natural number greater than 1 having more than two positive factors
options.B: A natural number greater than 1 having exactly two distinct positive factors: 1 and itself
options.C: Two or more integers whose HCF is 1
options.D: A number obtained by multiplying the given number by an integer

questions.explanation: A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 having exactly two distinct positive factors: 1 and itself.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the only even prime number?
questions.explanation: 2 is the only even prime number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a composite number?

options.A: A natural number greater than 1 having exactly two distinct positive factors
options.B: A natural number greater than 1 having more than two positive factors
options.C: An integer divisible by 2 without a remainder
options.D: Two or more integers whose HCF is 1

questions.explanation: A composite number is a natural number greater than 1 having more than two positive factors.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Is 1 prime or composite?

options.C: Neither; it has exactly one positive factor

questions.explanation: 1 is neither prime nor composite. It has exactly one positive factor.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are co-prime numbers?

options.A: Two or more integers whose HCF is 1; they need not themselves be prime
options.D: Numbers expressible as p/q where q ≠ 0

questions.explanation: Co-prime numbers are two or more integers whose HCF is 1; they need not themselves be prime.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a factor of a number?

options.A: A number obtained by multiplying the given number by an integer
options.B: A number that divides the given number exactly
options.C: The value contributed by a digit according to its position
options.D: The digit itself, irrespective of its position

questions.explanation: A factor of a number is a number that divides the given number exactly.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a multiple of a number?

options.A: A number that divides the given number exactly
options.B: A number obtained by multiplying the given number by an integer
options.C: The value contributed by a digit according to its position
options.D: The digit itself, irrespective of its position

questions.explanation: A multiple of a number is a number obtained by multiplying the given number by an integer.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the place value of a digit?

options.A: The digit itself, irrespective of its position
options.B: The value contributed by a digit according to its position; for example, 7 in 5,724 has place value 700
options.C: A number that divides the given number exactly
options.D: A number obtained by multiplying the given number by an integer

questions.explanation: The place value of a digit is the value contributed by a digit according to its position; for example, 7 in 5,724 has place value 700.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the face value of a digit?

options.A: The value contributed by a digit according to its position
options.B: The digit itself, irrespective of its position
options.C: A number that divides the given number exactly
options.D: A number obtained by multiplying the given number by an integer

questions.explanation: The face value of a digit is the digit itself, irrespective of its position.

questions.subject: Mathematics

options.A: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 2

options.C: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 2
options.D: The last digit must be 0 or 5

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 2 if the last digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the divisibility test for 3?

options.A: The last digit must be 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8
options.B: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 3
options.C: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 3
options.D: The last digit must be 0 or 5

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the divisibility test for 4?

options.A: The last digit must be 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8
options.B: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 4
options.C: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 4

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the divisibility test for 5?

options.A: The last digit must be 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8
options.B: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 5
options.C: The last digit must be 0 or 5
options.D: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 5

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 5 if the last digit is 0 or 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the divisibility test for 6?

options.A: The number must be divisible by both 2 and 3
options.B: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 6
options.C: The last digit must be 0 or 6
options.D: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 6

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 6 if it is divisible by both 2 and 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the divisibility test for 8?

options.A: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 8
options.B: The number formed by the last three digits must be divisible by 8
options.C: The last digit must be 0 or 8
options.D: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 8

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by the last three digits is divisible by 8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the divisibility test for 9?

options.A: The last digit must be 0 or 9
options.B: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 9
options.C: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 9
options.D: The number must be divisible by both 3 and 9

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the divisibility test for 10?

options.B: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 10
options.C: The last digit must be 0 or 5
options.D: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 10

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 10 if the last digit is 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the divisibility test for 11?

options.A: The last digit must be 0 or 1
options.B: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 11
options.C: The difference between the sums of alternate-position digits must be 0 or a multiple of 11
options.D: The number formed by the last three digits must be divisible by 11

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sums of alternate-position digits is 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the divisibility test for 12?

options.A: The number must be divisible by both 2 and 6
options.B: A number is divisible by 12 if it is divisible by both 3 and 4
options.C: The sum of the digits must be divisible by 12
options.D: The last two digits must be divisible by 12

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 12 if it is divisible by both 3 and 4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the remainder when a non-zero number is divided by itself?
questions.explanation: For a non-zero number, the remainder is 0 when divided by itself.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the remainder when a number is divided by 1?
questions.explanation: The remainder is 0 when a number is divided by 1.

questions.question: What is the value of any non-zero number raised to the power 0?
questions.explanation: Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 equals 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the value of 0 raised to a positive integer power?
questions.explanation: 0 raised to a positive integer power equals 0.

questions.question: What is the value of 0^0?

questions.question: What is the sign of the product of two numbers with the same sign?
questions.explanation: The product of two numbers with the same sign is positive.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the sign of the product of two numbers with opposite signs?
questions.explanation: The product of two numbers with opposite signs is negative.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the sign of the quotient of two numbers with the same sign?

options.A: Positive, provided the divisor is non-zero
options.B: Negative, provided the divisor is non-zero

questions.explanation: The quotient of two numbers with the same sign is positive, provided the divisor is non-zero.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the sign of the quotient of two numbers with opposite signs?

options.A: Positive, provided the divisor is non-zero
options.B: Negative, provided the divisor is non-zero

questions.explanation: The quotient of two numbers with opposite signs is negative, provided the divisor is non-zero.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the absolute value of a number?

options.B: Its distance from zero on the number line; it is never negative. For example, |-8| = 8

questions.explanation: The absolute value of a number is its distance from zero on the number line; it is never negative. For example, |-8| = 8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is simplification?

options.A: Reducing a numerical expression to its simplest value by applying arithmetic operations in the correct order
options.B: Finding the HCF of two numbers
options.C: Converting a fraction to a decimal
options.D: Calculating the average of a set of numbers

questions.explanation: Simplification is reducing a numerical expression to its simplest value by applying arithmetic operations in the correct order.

options.B: Brackets, Operations, Decimals, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction
options.C: Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Summation
options.D: Basic Operations, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the correct rule when division and multiplication occur together?

options.C: Perform them from left to right because they have equal precedence

questions.explanation: Division and multiplication have equal precedence, so they must be performed from left to right.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the correct rule when addition and subtraction occur together?

options.C: Perform them from left to right because they have equal precedence

questions.explanation: Addition and subtraction have equal precedence, so they must be performed from left to right.

questions.question: How should nested brackets be simplified?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What does a vinculum mean in simplification?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How is a fraction divided by another fraction?

options.A: Multiply the numerators and denominators separately
options.B: Multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction, provided the second fraction is non-zero
options.D: Add the fractions and then divide

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the square of a sum?
questions.explanation: The square of a sum is (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the square of a difference?
questions.explanation: The square of a difference is (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the difference of two squares?
questions.explanation: The difference of two squares is a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the product identity for (a + b)(a - b)?
questions.explanation: The product identity for (a + b)(a - b) is a^2 - b^2.

questions.question: How should an expression such as 18 ÷ 3 × 2 be evaluated?

options.C: Division first: 18 ÷ 3 = 6, then 6 × 2 = 12, but only if brackets are absent

questions.question: What is a common simplification error involving BODMAS?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the HCF (Highest Common Factor)?

options.A: The smallest positive integer that is a multiple of each of the given non-zero integers
options.B: The greatest positive integer that divides each of the given integers exactly
options.C: The product of the given integers
options.D: The sum of the given integers

questions.explanation: The HCF (Highest Common Factor) is the greatest positive integer that divides each of the given integers exactly; it is also called GCD.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the LCM (Lowest Common Multiple)?

options.A: The greatest positive integer that divides each of the given integers exactly
options.B: The smallest positive integer that is a multiple of each of the given non-zero integers
options.C: The product of the given integers
options.D: The sum of the given integers

questions.explanation: The LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) is the smallest positive integer that is a multiple of each of the given non-zero integers.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How can HCF be found by prime factorisation?

options.A: Write each number as a product of primes and multiply every prime factor appearing, using the greatest power of each
options.B: Write each number as a product of primes and multiply only the common prime factors, using the smallest power of each
options.C: Multiply all the given numbers together
options.D: Add all the given numbers together

questions.explanation: To find HCF by prime factorisation, write each number as a product of primes and multiply only the common prime factors, using the smallest power of each.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How can LCM be found by prime factorisation?

options.A: Write each number as a product of primes and multiply only the common prime factors, using the smallest power of each
options.B: Write each number as a product of primes and multiply every prime factor appearing, using the greatest power of each
options.C: Multiply all the given numbers together
options.D: Add all the given numbers together

questions.explanation: To find LCM by prime factorisation, write each number as a product of primes and multiply every prime factor appearing, using the greatest power of each.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the HCF of 12 and 18?
questions.explanation: The common factors of 12 and 18 are 1, 2, 3 and 6, and 6 is the greatest. Hence HCF = 6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
questions.explanation: 36 is the smallest positive number divisible by both 12 and 18.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the relationship between HCF and LCM of two positive integers?

options.A: HCF + LCM = product of the two numbers
options.B: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers
options.C: HCF × LCM = sum of the two numbers
options.D: HCF ÷ LCM = product of the two numbers

questions.explanation: For positive integers a and b: HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Does the HCF-LCM product rule apply directly to three or more numbers?

options.B: No. The simple product identity is guaranteed for two positive integers; do not extend it directly to three or more
options.C: Yes, but only for prime numbers
options.D: Yes, but only for even numbers

questions.explanation: The simple product identity is guaranteed for two positive integers; do not extend it directly to three or more numbers.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the HCF of two co-prime numbers?
questions.explanation: The HCF of two co-prime numbers is 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the LCM of two co-prime positive integers a and b?
questions.explanation: The LCM of two co-prime positive integers a and b is a × b.

questions.question: If one positive integer exactly divides another, what is their HCF?
questions.explanation: If one positive integer exactly divides another, their HCF is the smaller number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If one positive integer exactly divides another, what is their LCM?
questions.explanation: If one positive integer exactly divides another, their LCM is the larger number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How can HCF of large numbers be found using Euclid's algorithm?

options.A: Multiply the numbers and divide by 2
options.B: Repeatedly divide the larger number by the smaller; replace the pair with the divisor and remainder; continue until the remainder is zero. The last non-zero divisor is the HCF
options.C: Add the numbers and find the square root
options.D: Subtract the smaller number from the larger until both are equal

questions.explanation: Euclid's algorithm: repeatedly divide the larger number by the smaller; replace the pair with the divisor and remainder; continue until the remainder is zero. The last non-zero divisor is the HCF.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How can HCF be used in problems involving the greatest possible equal groups?

options.A: Find the LCM of the quantities
options.B: Find the HCF of the quantities, because the largest equal group size must divide every quantity
options.C: Find the average of the quantities
options.D: Find the sum of the quantities

questions.explanation: In problems involving the greatest possible equal groups, find the HCF of the quantities, because the largest equal group size must divide every quantity.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How can LCM be used in problems involving events repeating together?

options.A: Find the HCF of the time intervals
options.B: Find the LCM of the time intervals; it gives the first positive time at which the events coincide again
options.C: Find the average of the time intervals
options.D: Find the sum of the time intervals

questions.explanation: In problems involving events repeating together, find the LCM of the time intervals; it gives the first positive time at which the events coincide again.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the HCF of 0 and a positive integer n?

options.C: n, under the standard convention gcd(0,n) = |n|

questions.explanation: Under the standard convention, gcd(0,n) = |n|. So the HCF of 0 and a positive integer n is n.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the LCM of 0 and a positive integer?
questions.explanation: The LCM of 0 and a positive integer is usually defined as 0 in the standard non-negative convention; school word problems generally use LCM of positive integers.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a fraction?

options.A: A number representing part of a whole or a quotient, written a/b with b ≠ 0; a is the numerator and b is the denominator
options.B: A number whose denominator is a power of 10
options.C: A number consisting of a whole number and a proper fraction
options.D: The multiplicative inverse of a non-zero number

questions.explanation: A fraction represents part of a whole or a quotient, written a/b with b ≠ 0; a is the numerator and b is the denominator.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a proper fraction?

options.A: A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its positive denominator
options.B: A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its positive denominator; its value is less than 1
options.D: A fraction whose denominator is a power of 10

questions.explanation: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its positive denominator; its value is less than 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is an improper fraction?

options.A: A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its positive denominator
options.B: A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its positive denominator; its value is at least 1
options.D: A fraction whose denominator is a power of 10

questions.explanation: An improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to its positive denominator; its value is at least 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a mixed fraction?

options.A: A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator
options.B: A number consisting of a whole number and a proper fraction, such as 2 1/3
options.D: A fraction whose denominator is a power of 10

questions.explanation: A mixed fraction is a number consisting of a whole number and a proper fraction, such as 2 1/3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How is a mixed fraction converted into an improper fraction?

options.A: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and add the denominator
options.B: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and place the result over the original denominator
options.C: Add the whole number to the numerator and place over the denominator
options.D: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the whole number

questions.explanation: To convert a mixed fraction into an improper fraction: multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and place the result over the original denominator.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are equivalent fractions?

options.B: Fractions having the same value, obtained by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number
options.D: Fractions whose denominator is a power of 10

questions.explanation: Equivalent fractions have the same value, obtained by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How are fractions added or subtracted with unlike denominators?

options.D: Find the HCF of the denominators

questions.question: How are fractions multiplied?

options.D: Multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second

questions.explanation: To multiply fractions: multiply the numerators together and the denominators together; simplify the result.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How are fractions divided?

options.A: Multiply the numerators and denominators separately
options.B: Multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction

questions.explanation: To divide fractions: multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction.

questions.question: What is a reciprocal?

options.A: The additive inverse of a non-zero number
options.B: The multiplicative inverse of a non-zero number; the reciprocal of a/b is b/a
options.D: The absolute value of a number

questions.explanation: A reciprocal is the multiplicative inverse of a non-zero number; the reciprocal of a/b is b/a.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a unit fraction?

options.A: A fraction with numerator 1, such as 1/7
options.B: A fraction whose denominator is a power of 10
options.C: A fraction whose numerator is greater than its denominator
options.D: A number consisting of a whole number and a proper fraction

questions.explanation: A unit fraction is a fraction with numerator 1, such as 1/7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a decimal fraction?

options.B: A fraction whose denominator is a power of 10, such as 37/100
options.C: A fraction whose numerator is greater than its denominator
options.D: A number consisting of a whole number and a proper fraction

questions.explanation: A decimal fraction is a fraction whose denominator is a power of 10, such as 37/100.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a terminating decimal?

options.A: A decimal in which one digit or a group of digits repeats indefinitely
options.B: A decimal representation that ends after a finite number of digits, such as 0.125
options.C: A decimal that cannot be expressed as a fraction
options.D: A decimal whose denominator is not a power of 10

questions.explanation: A terminating decimal is a decimal representation that ends after a finite number of digits, such as 0.125.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a recurring decimal?

options.A: A decimal representation that ends after a finite number of digits
options.B: A decimal in which one digit or a group of digits repeats indefinitely, such as 0.333...
options.C: A decimal that cannot be expressed as a fraction
options.D: A decimal with no decimal point

questions.explanation: A recurring decimal is a decimal in which one digit or a group of digits repeats indefinitely, such as 0.333...

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: When does a rational number have a terminating decimal in lowest terms?

options.B: When its denominator has prime factors other than 2 and 5

questions.explanation: Before comparing quantities in a ratio, convert them to the same unit.

questions.question: How is a ratio simplified?

options.B: Divide all terms by their HCF

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is an equivalent ratio?

options.C: A ratio obtained by subtracting the same number from all terms

questions.explanation: An equivalent ratio is obtained by multiplying or dividing all its terms by the same non-zero number.

questions.question: What is the product rule of a proportion?

options.B: If a:b = c:d, then ad = bc
options.C: If a:b = c:d, then ab = cd
options.D: If a:b = c:d, then a + b = c + d

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are the extremes in a:b = c:d?

questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.question: What is direct proportion?

questions.explanation: Two quantities are directly proportional when their ratio remains constant; if one increases by a factor, the other increases by the same factor.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is inverse proportion?

options.B: Two quantities are inversely proportional when their product remains constant; if one increases by a factor, the other decreases by the same factor

questions.question: If 6 workers complete a fixed job in 10 days, how long will 12 equally efficient workers take?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the percentage-point difference?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the arithmetic average (mean)?

options.A: The product of all observations divided by the number of observations

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is cost price (CP)?

options.A: The amount for which an item is sold
options.B: The amount paid to acquire or produce an item, including relevant costs where specified

options.D: The reduction given on the marked price

questions.explanation: Cost price (CP) is the amount paid to acquire or produce an item, including relevant costs where specified.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is selling price (SP)?

options.A: The amount paid to acquire or produce an item
options.B: The amount for which an item is sold
options.C: The price displayed or listed before discount
options.D: The reduction given on the marked price

questions.explanation: Selling price (SP) is the amount for which an item is sold.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is profit?

options.A: Profit occurs when CP is greater than SP; profit = CP - SP
options.B: Profit occurs when SP is greater than CP; profit = SP - CP

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is loss?

options.B: Loss occurs when CP is greater than SP; loss = CP - SP

questions.explanation: Loss occurs when CP is greater than SP; loss = CP - SP.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: On which value is profit percentage generally calculated?
questions.explanation: Profit percentage is generally calculated on cost price. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: On which value is loss percentage generally calculated?
questions.explanation: Loss percentage is generally calculated on cost price. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the selling price after a profit of p%?
questions.explanation: The selling price after a profit of p% is SP = CP × (100 + p)/100.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the selling price after a loss of d%?
questions.explanation: The selling price after a loss of d% is SP = CP × (100 - d)/100.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is marked price (MP)?

options.A: The amount paid to acquire an item

options.D: The reduction given on the marked price

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is discount?

options.A: The reduction given on the marked price; discount = MP - SP
options.B: The reduction given on the cost price; discount = CP - SP
options.C: The profit earned on an item
options.D: The loss incurred on an item

questions.explanation: Discount is the reduction given on the marked price; discount = MP - SP.

questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is simple interest (SI)?

options.B: Interest calculated only on the original principal throughout the period
options.C: Interest calculated on the total amount

questions.explanation: Simple interest (SI) is interest calculated only on the original principal throughout the period.

questions.question: What is the formula for simple interest?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is compound interest (CI)?

options.B: Interest calculated on the principal plus accumulated interest from earlier compounding periods
options.C: Interest calculated on the total amount only
options.D: Interest calculated at a fixed rate

questions.explanation: Compound interest (CI) is interest calculated on the principal plus accumulated interest from earlier compounding periods.

questions.question: What is the formula for annual compound interest?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the amount in an interest problem?

questions.subject: Mathematics

options.B: A decrease in value over time, often calculated by compound percentage decrease

options.D: The total amount of a loan

questions.explanation: Depreciation is a decrease in value over time, often calculated by compound percentage decrease.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If A completes a job in x days and B in y days, what is their combined one-day work?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a proper fraction?

options.A: A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its positive denominator
options.B: A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its positive denominator; its value is less than 1
options.D: A fraction whose denominator is a power of 10

questions.explanation: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its positive denominator; its value is less than 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is an improper fraction?

options.A: A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its positive denominator
options.B: A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its positive denominator; its value is at least 1
options.D: A fraction whose denominator is a power of 10

questions.explanation: An improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to its positive denominator; its value is at least 1.

options.D: A fraction whose denominator is a power of 10

questions.explanation: A mixed fraction is a number consisting of a whole number and a proper fraction, such as 2 1/3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What are equivalent fractions?
